messages:
sarah.ae: Heads-up — incoming POC with a large fintech client asking for a drop-in migration from VelvetAPI. They want prompt parity, predictable latency, and answers to the security questionnaire. Can we triage blockers?

natalie.solutions: Noted. I started a POC checklist: billing, latency targets, security Qs, sample prompts, and a parity eval harness. I'll paste link in a sec.

cheng_runtime: Quick Q — are they using Velvet's streaming completions + role-based chat? That affects how we map endpoints.

sarah.ae: Yes, streaming chat with a few custom system messages. Also they use a couple of Velvet-specific meta-fields in responses (like `deterministic_score`). Need guidance on mapping.

liam_perf: From infra side, typical migration pain: different tokenization, KV-cache behavior, and batching defaults causing latency variance. We should capture 95th perc p99 for their sample workload.

natalie.solutions: Link: https://redwood.internal/pocs/velvet-migration-2026 (internal). I added a section for pricing scenarios — self-serve hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private.

sec-bot: Security questionnaire posted to the thread: https://redwood.internal/sec/q/velvet-poc. Items flagged: SSO/SAML, data residency, SOC2 attestation, customer-managed KMS.

cheng_runtime: For the compat shim, propose mapping Velvet's `completions.create` -> Redwood `generate` and Velvet chat messages -> our `chat` with a shim that preserves `deterministic_score` as a heuristic field. Example transform:```js
// pseudo-transform
function velvetToRedwood(req){
  const system = req.messages.find(m => m.role === 'system')?.content || '';
  return {
    mode: 'chat',
    system_prompt: system,
    user_prompt: req.messages.filter(m=>m.role!=='system').map(m=>m.content).join('\n'),
    stream: req.stream === true
  };
}
```

liam_perf: Also run tests with our batching=auto vs batching=min_latency to see throughput/latency tradeoffs. I'll add a perf matrix in the POC doc.

natalie.solutions: Pricing note for sales — for short POC (<30 days, demo scale) we can offer Hosted credits. For pilot at production traffic, recommend Dedicated with monthly commit. I'll add example cost calc: tokens/day * 30 * model-rate +- safety buffer.

sarah.ae: The customer is asking if any output diffs will be expected (they want deterministic parity). How do we set expectations?

cheng_runtime: Full determinism is unlikely across different runtimes/quantization. Our approach: 1) reproduce their prompt pipeline (tokenization + system prompts) 2) provide a regression harness using embeddings to detect semantic drift and a side-by-side sampling comparison. Recommend signing up for an eval window to iterate.

liam_perf: For regression harness, use a dataset of ~500 representative prompts, measure:
- embedding cosine similarity distribution
- response length delta
- answer overlap on anchor questions
I'll run a baseline comparison and drop results into the POC doc.

sec-bot: Customer asked about SOC2 and SSO. Current state: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and supports SAML SSO on Private + Dedicated enterprise plans. KMS integrations available for Private.

natalie.solutions: I'll compile a one-page SLA + security summary we can hand to their procurement. SLA highlights: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated, support SLAs for escalations, and dedicated onboarding assistance.

cheng_runtime: I can scaffold a minimal compat repo this afternoon and push to internal git: git.redwood/velvet-bridge. It will include the transform above + sample tests that assert token-level mapping.

sarah.ae: Amazing. Can we assign owners & ETA?

natalie.solutions: I'll own customer comms and security Q follow-up — ETA EOD tomorrow for the summary.

cheng_runtime: I'll have the repo stub + transform + one sample test by EOD today.

liam_perf: I'll run perf matrix and give p50/p95/p99 for both batching configs by EOD tomorrow.

sec-bot: Security doc updated with required artifacts list (audit logs, IAM mappings, KMS config).

sarah.ae: Thanks team. Next sync scheduled Thu 10am PT with customer. @natalie.solutions @cheng_runtime @liam_perf please bring the POC doc, repo link, and perf numbers. I'll send calendar invite. :thumbsup:

cheng_runtime: Will do. Also note: we should add a short note in the POC that model-level quantization differences can change response phrasing — helps reset expectations.

natalie.solutions: Added that note.

sarah.ae: Great. Closing this thread for now — will re-open after Thu call with the customer's feedback.
